user_stories.title: USX1 - Colander quick deploy
user_stories.body: Deploying a full Colander instance currently requires a public-facing IP address and a level of infrastructure expertise that places it out of reach for many potential users. To address this, we will develop a lightweight, self-contained quick-run deployment script allowing practitioners to spin up a local Colander instance with minimal configuration. Our main goal is to make it easier to discover, try, test, contribute and deploy the PTS stack (Colander, Threatr, ...). To achieve this we will rework how those tools are deployed and packaged so that users will have the smallest learning curve possible. We will be as less specific as possible so that users feel comfortable and can focus on the tools rather than how to get things done. We will also offer to users an easy way to deploy the whole stack or only one of the PTS tools (so a user will be able to deploy a Threatr instance without Colander if they wish, as an example). We expect that more people will be able to discover those tools, trying more easily by themselves, and we want to drastically lower the barrier to entry.

user_stories.title: US1 - PiRogue VPN
user_stories.body:
**Description:** The PiRogue VPN project aims to facilitate the operational effectiveness of organizations in assisting individuals at risk. By deploying PiRogue as [an emergency VPN](https://www.civilsphereproject.org/emergency-vpn) server, people at risk can easily connect their device and security analysts can analyze the network traffic of the device. Alerts and DPI data will be sent to Colander for further analysis, and the management of both virtual and physical PiRogues will be centralized through Colander. This activity mainly consists in integrating [Wireguard](https://www.wireguard.com/). This feature will allow users at risk who do not have a physical PiRogue to get their phone’s network traffic analyzed by any organization running a PiRogue VPN service. The end-user simply has to install the Wireguard app on their device and flash the QR-code provided by the organization running the service.

user_stories.title: USX2 - Documentation restructure
user_stories.body: The current PTS documentation, while technically accurate, is oriented toward expert users and assumes familiarity with underlying concepts. Over the extension period, we will restructure the documentation from the ground up, organizing it around concrete use cases and practitioner workflows rather than technical components. Each major use case will receive a dedicated, plain-language guide accessible to non-technical folks for civil society organizations and practitioners. This work builds on findings from the most recent The Engine Room report and reflects feedback consistently raised by community members.

user_stories.title: US2 - Better knowledge management
user_stories.body:
**Description:** A significant improvement involves refining knowledge organization and representation within Colander. This includes establishing a hierarchical structure for cases, where parent cases inherit from child cases, enhancing the management of extensive investigations. Furthermore, Colander will support the creation of multiple graphs within a single case, allowing for diverse projections of a subset of the case knowledge graph. The inclusion of thumbnails on graph nodes will simplify the investigation by involving pictures.

user_stories.title: USX3 - Workshops preparation
user_stories.body: We will develop a complete, ready-to-deliver workshop curriculum covering PiRogue, Colander, and dynamic Android application analysis using Octopus. This includes slide preparation and supporting materials for each module, as well as a hands-on practical cases built around PiRogue and a Colander environment. The goal is to produce a reusable, facilitator-ready package that enables both in-person and remote training delivery for human rights organizations and digital security trainers.

user_stories.title: US3 - Interoperability
user_stories.body:
**Description:** The project seeks to enhance interoperability by enabling the import and export of knowledge in industry-standard format. This includes batch importing of knowledge, data interchange in MISP format, and the support for user-defined templates to generate custom knowledge feeds. PTS users must have the freedom to move their data and findings from and to other tools such as [OpenCTI](https://docs.opencti.io/latest/) or [MISP](https://www.misp-project.org/).

user_stories.title: US4 - Evidence collection
user_stories.body:
**Description:** Efforts will be directed towards the extraction and preservation of artifacts and evidence, particularly those extracted from online content and mobile devices. The system will automatically archive and index various forms of online content such as photos, videos, social media posts, and web pages. Additionally, the capability of saving a watermarked capture or recording of the victim’s phone screen will be added to the PiRogue. In the context of forensic analysis, it is crucial to not only collect potential evidence of a compromise but also collect its  context, such as the attack vector. As an example, retrieving and storing tweets was key in the [Citizen Lab investigation on Predator](https://citizenlab.ca/2023/10/predator-spyware-targets-us-eu-lawmakers-journalists/), retrieving and storing WhatsApp messages in the [Citizen Lab investigation on Tibetan groups being targeted](https://citizenlab.ca/2019/09/poison-carp-tibetan-groups-targeted-with-1-click-mobile-exploits/).

user_stories.title: US6 - Third-Party Intelligence
user_stories.body: **Description:** This project aims to enhance intelligence gathering by integrating it with well-known third-party sources. This includes an integration of _ScarletShark_ and _Shodan_ and retrieving intelligence data from them. During the analysis of forensic dumps and extracted files from a potentially compromised device, analysts collect IOCs (Indicator Of Compromise). It is crucial for analysts to easily gather threat intelligence from 3rd-parties. As an example, one identifies a potential malicious network communication with a specific domain name, the next logical step is to know what has already been documented about it.

user_stories.title: US10 - Censorship resilience
user_stories.body: **Description**: This work package addresses a structural gap in the current deployment model. The communities with the greatest need for mobile security tooling are often located in jurisdictions where governments actively filter or disrupt internet access. This workstream implements access mechanisms designed for those environments, with a specific focus on the Eurasia region, so that network-level interference does not become a barrier to PTS adoption or operational use by at-risk groups.

tasks.title: D2-1 establish redundant distribution mirrors
tasks.body:
**Description**: GitHub as PTS's sole distribution channel is a single point of failure: it can be blocked, rate-limited, or hit by platform actions outside our control. This work package establishes redundant channels so PTS stays installable even if GitHub becomes unavailable.

**Approach**: 
* Set up a secondary APT-compatible package repository (PPA), hosted independently of GitHub, and integrate it into the existing build pipeline so it receives every release automatically.
* Mirror all active PTS Git repositories to Codeberg, or alternatively to a self-hosted Forgejo/Gitea instance, with automated synchronization triggered on every push to the primary repository.
* Set up a secondary container registry (e.g., Quay.io or a self-hosted registry) and integrate it into the CI/CD pipeline so every released image is automatically pushed to both registries.

tasks.title: D2-2 PTS services are accessible over Tor
tasks.body:
**Description**: Colander and Threatr typically run on the open internet, exposing availability and users' connections to censorship, precisely the threat model PTS investigates. 

**Approach**: Deploy Colander and Threatr as Tor hidden services, so both can be reached directly via .onion addresses. In deployments where Colander connects to a separately-hosted Threatr instance, route that Colander-to-Threatr connection over Tor as well, so no part of the data path depends on the clearnet.

tasks.title: D2-3 censorship resilient deployment
tasks.body:
**Description**: This work package removes dependencies on unrestricted internet access so that installing, updating, and running PTS remains possible even when a user's network is actively censored.

**Approach**: 
* Package the Grafana plugins required by PiRogue into a Debian package, so they are installed directly from PTS's own package repository rather than fetched from Grafana's external plugin registry at install time.
* Develop an APT transport method that can fall back to established censorship-circumvention tools, such as Outline, Algo, or Xray.
* Route all internal Colander platform network traffic over a WireGuard VPN, so internal communications are encrypted end-to-end and encapsulated in traffic that is harder to fingerprint or selectively block.

user_stories.title: US11 - Security hardening
user_stories.body: **Description**: This workstream will implement security controls to align with security governance standards, establishing a defensible security posture appropriate for a platform handling sensitive data from civil society partners.

tasks.title: D3-1 stack monitoring
tasks.body:
**Description**: PTS handles sensitive case data, yet Colander currently lacks the logging and audit trails needed to detect compromise. This work package builds an observability stack around it.

**Approach**: Instrument Colander with a modern observability stack: Sentry for application error tracking, VictoriaMetrics and Grafana Alloy for metrics collection using the OpenMetrics data format, and Loki for centralized log aggregation, with Grafana as the shared visualization and alerting layer across all three.

tasks.title: D3-2 vulnerability scanning
tasks.body:
**Description**: PTS's third-party dependencies are not currently checked against vulnerability databases, and a dependency can become vulnerable the day after it's added. This work package puts continuous vulnerability detection into the build pipeline.

**Approach**: Integrate an automated dependency-scanning tool (e.g. Dependabot, Trivy, or OSV-Scanner) into the CI/CD pipeline so every commit and pull request is checked against known vulnerability databases, with alerts routed to maintainers and, where feasible, automated patch pull requests for flagged dependencies.

tasks.title: D3-3 user authentication & authorization
tasks.body:
**Description**: Colander's access control was built for single-organization deployments, not multi-organization use: authentication uses manual Django accounts, and object-level permissions are inconsistent across data types. This work package rebuilds it on modern, auditable foundations.

**Approach**: 
* Extend Colander's authentication to support signing in via external identity providers (e.g. Google, GitHub, Keycloak) using Django Allauth.
* Reimplement object-level authorization using Django Guardian or a comparable framework, applying a single, consistent permission model across all Colander object types.
* Implement automatic detection of repeated failed authentication attempts from the same source, with configurable thresholds that trigger temporary throttling or lockout of the offending source.

tasks.title: D3-4 secrets management
tasks.body:
**Description**: Storing Colander secrets improperly creates a single point of failure, anyone with server read access gains the keys to impersonate the platform or undermine evidence integrity. This work package moves secrets management into hardened infrastructure.

**Approach**: Deploy a PKCS#11-compliant secrets management service (e.g. HashiCorp Vault, or a hardware/software security module exposing a PKCS#11 interface) to generate, store, and serve Colander's cryptographic secrets, so that signing and other sensitive operations are performed through the service rather than by exposing raw key material to the application.

user_stories.title: US12 - System engineering and administration
user_stories.body: **Description**: The continuous infrastructure management keeps production systems stable and available through routine operational tasks, monitoring, and environment integrity checks, improving service reliability for hosted users and enhancing deployment packages for organizations that self-host their PTS stack.

tasks.title: D4-1 recurring system administration activities
tasks.body:
**Description**: This task includes the following activities:
* the maintenance of our infrastructure hosting Colander servers
* the update deployment playbooks and system administration documentation

tasks.title: D4-2 Kubernetes deployment support
tasks.body:
**Description**: Many organizations adopting Colander standardize on Kubernetes, which its current deployment model doesn't support. This work package removes that barrier.

**Approach**: Package Colander and its dependent services (database, task queue, storage, etc.) as Kubernetes-native resources, Helm chart or equivalent manifests, covering configuration, secrets, persistent storage, scaling, and health checks needed for a production-grade deployment.

tasks.title: D4-3 PiRogue isolation
tasks.body:
**Description**: The PiRogue VPN currently runs monolithically on its host, so any compromise or crash can affect the entire service. Containerization limits the blast radius and improves portability.

**Approach**: Package the PiRogue VPN as one or more OCI-compatible containers (e.g. using Podman or Docker), isolating it from the host system and other services while preserving the network access it needs to function as a VPN.

user_stories.title: US13 - Interoperability
user_stories.body: **Description**: Compatibility with formats like STIX 2 and MISP is maintained as a commitment, ensuring that intelligence produced and consumed through PTS remains compatible with the ecosystem of tools and workflows used by organizations. Preserving interoperability reduces friction for adoption and makes the collective capacity for threat sharing stronger.

tasks.title: D5-1 interoperability with external services
tasks.body:
**Description**: Most PTS users already run ticketing systems and threat intelligence platforms. This work package extends PTS's ability to push data outward and keeps threat intelligence connectors current.

**Approach**: 
* Implement configurable inbound webhook support in Colander, allowing operators to define event triggers (e.g. new case, new artifact, status change) and the external endpoints that should be notified, with payloads structured to integrate cleanly with common ticketing platforms.
* Review and update Threatr's existing connectors against the current APIs of the services they integrate with, bringing each connector back in line with present-day endpoints, authentication methods, and response formats.

tasks.title: D5-2 data portability
tasks.body:
**Description**: Investigators need to share findings between tools and partners. This work package keeps PTS's support for the two dominant open standards conformant.

**Approach**: Establish a validation process (including automated test fixtures covering representative case data) to verify that STIX 2 and MISP import/export in PTS remain conformant with the current versions of both standards, and correct any discrepancies found.

user_stories.title: US100 - Documentation
user_stories.body: **Description:** Documenting the project is key in its usability. We are continuously documenting the different tools and features we develop and build new learning materials to facilitate skills development.

user_stories.title: US101 - Software maintenance
user_stories.body: **Description**: Outdated dependencies carry unpatched vulnerabilities; unmaintained images eventually stop working. This work package encompasses support of core PTS components through timely updates, bug resolution, and dependency management, with particular emphasis on security updates.

tasks.title: D1-1 maintenance
tasks.body:
**Description**: This task includes the following activities:
* the reduction of the technical debt
* the update of the Debian packages
* the update the Debian OS image

tasks.title: D1-2 support Debian 13
tasks.body: **Description**: Rebase PiRogue OS onto Debian 13 (Trixie), updating package dependencies, configuration, and build processes as needed to ensure full compatibility, and validate the resulting image across supported PiRogue hardware.

tasks.title: D1-3 support Debian 14
tasks.body: **Description**: Rebase PiRogue OS onto Debian 14 (Forky), updating package dependencies, configuration, and build processes as needed to ensure full compatibility, and validate the resulting image across supported PiRogue hardware.

tasks.title: D1-4 testing and qualification setup
tasks.body:
**Description**: PiRogue's three deployment modes (Appliance, Access Point, VPN) each require a separate build, and validating a single feature currently involves a long sequence of manual steps per mode. This work package automates that pipeline.

**Approach**: Create a build toolset (e.g. Makefile-based) that orchestrates virtualization tools like QEMU to automate the full validation pipeline, compiling dependencies, packaging artifacts, provisioning the correct target-specific VM for each deployment mode, and running functional tests, replacing the current sequence of manual steps with a single, repeatable, automated workflow.

tasks.title: D1-5 support Web extension Manifest v3
tasks.body:
**Description**: Browsers are phasing out Manifest V2, but Colander Companion still runs on it. This work package migrates it ahead of a browser-side deadline outside PTS's control.

**Approach**: Migrate Colander Companion to Manifest V3, updating its background script model (service workers instead of persistent background pages), permissions handling, and any APIs affected by the V2-to-V3 transition, while preserving existing functionality.

user_stories.title: US102 - Community and outreach
user_stories.body:
**Description**: Given the success of events, webinars and demos with members of the civil society, NGOs and security researchers, we continue with our outreach plan. We organize trainings and demonstration sessions as well as creating spaces for the community to share feedback and request new features via our mailing list, GitHub issues or Discord server.
We analyze one Android app that has received the community's interest (ex COP28 app) per month. The application to be analyzed is chosen by the community. The analysis report is first privately shared with the community and one month later it is publicly released.

We organize monthly calls open to all members of the community to share project updates and get the community’s feedback.
